TWO ECONOMIES, DELIBERATELY SEVERED

Most crypto games are built as a pipe: farm the game, convert your farm to the token, sell. Then every payout the designers add is quietly a decision about the token, and the only way to keep the token steady is to make the game stingy. OMERTÀ doesn't have the pipe. Street cash cannot become $OMR — at any price, through any route. Cash is the game's blood: a hundred hustles, rackets, fronts, heists, the casino, the track. It buys, bribes, arms and builds — and it stops there.

What that severing buys is the rest of the design. Grinding harder can't inflate the token, so the game is free to be generous where a game should be generous. Grinding creates no $OMR — there is no wage, no yield and no drip. What can mint it is a short enumerated list a nightly job checks: the mission ladder pays a bit over a thousand across a whole career, and the rest are issued only when a real token arrives to back them, one for one. Nobody farms it into existence — which is exactly why the $OMR in the city is worth taking off somebody. And the one conversion that exists runs the other way: burn $OMR at the Window for cash, out of a till that real sinks paid for — a claim on money that already exists, never a promise, refusing cleanly when it's dry.

It also settles a question this particular game had to answer. OMERTÀ is about risk: your street can be killed, your empire seized, your cash looted off your body. A currency that was an exit from that risk would undo the game it lives in. Severed, $OMR isn't the escape hatch from the streets — it's the thing you take to the streets. Every dollar and every $OMR lives on a built-in ledger, honest to the cent, with a conservation sweep running against it every night. $OMR buys real advantage — a ladder of carry, capacity and a better fence, climbed by HOLDING it rather than spending it. What it does not buy is a higher ceiling: the top of that ladder is reachable without paying a cent, and nothing on it helps you fight. A whale who buys in gets there sooner. A sharp player with empty pockets still gets there — and can take the whale's $OMR off his body.

THE LAY OF THE LAND

Respect / Level
Your standing. Respect is XP; your level is derived from it and gates every job, path, and perk.
Nerve
What crime costs. It's the clock on the street loop — jobs are gated by nerve, not energy, so a grinding session is paced by how fast nerve trickles back.
Energy
What the physical work costs: the gym, boosting cars, heist crews, cartel raids, convoy ambushes, shakedowns, races. If your energy bar sits full, that's not idle capacity — it's content you haven't touched yet.
Health / Hospital
Lose a fight and you're under the Doc's care for a spell — that's protection, not prison: rivals can't jump or shoot you, but you can still run jobs and your businesses. Hit zero in the wrong fight and you're dead.
Heat / The Law
Crime draws heat. Enough of it and the Bureau opens a RICO case — see The Law tab. Lay low or bribe to cool it.
Cash vs. the Bank vs. $OMR
Pocket cash can be looted when you're killed. Banked cash is safer (but takes time to clear). $OMR is the premium, extractable currency — redeemed for cash at the Exchange window, one way.
Omertà
The code of silence — your family won't hunt you, and you can't contract a made brother… unless they turn rat.
The Kitchen / Deal
Cook product, hire a crew, and move weight — the deepest cash engine. Watch the heat and the nut (crew wages).
Going Legit
What your earned $OMR does: stake it for real power (the ladder), redeem it for cash at the Window, claim backed ETH at the Vault — or get Made and take it out on-chain. The endgame.
Prestige / The Heir
Death isn't the end of your account — your heir inherits prestige, $OMR, your estate, and your standing with the fixers. Only the street resets: stats, skills, businesses, crew.
Safehouse
Pay to go to ground — untouchable by hits for a few hours. A shield, not a bunker: you can't run offense or move money from inside. Cost scales with your wealth.
Wanted / Welsher
Stiff a loan and you're a welsher — nobody lends to you again (square your name at the Shylock). Default under pursuit and you're wanted: even your own family can hunt you, and NPC guns come looking.
The Law / Indicted
Heat builds a case. Cross the line and the Bureau indicts you — a RICO trial that can seize your pocket and bank (staked $OMR and minted gear are safe). Bribe, retain a lawyer, pay the envelope, or lay low before it files.
The Pen
Jail is a place. Work the yard to shave your sentence, buy protection, bribe a guard, or shank a rival who's inside with you — then break out and run as a fugitive.
In transit / Unbonding
Fresh bank deposits and just-unstaked $OMR sit exposed for a window — a killer loots them. Wait for cash to clear and $OMR to finish unbonding before you count it safe.
Skills
Every four levels you earn a skill point. Spend them in The Life on a branch — Enforcer, Operator, or Wheelman — for permanent edges. They die with your street.
The Family / Turf / Commission
Join a family for backup, turf income, and wars. Tribute is what you kick up; the Commission is the five biggest families setting the week's rules.
Vendetta
Kill a man and his bloodline swears a blood feud against yours. Settle it with revenge inside the window for feared respect. Kill them again and it DEEPENS (Vendetta → Blood Feud → War of Extinction — a longer window). Or hold a sit-down and both lines bury it in peace.
The Underworld
Named fixers — the Doc, Vinnie, Bella, Big Tuna, the Madame. Earn their standing by working their corner of the game for discounts and favors. Cross them and they hold a grudge.
The Pad / Cold
A front's upkeep — protection and wages, owed every hour whether the place earns or not. The till only holds a day's take; the pad keeps running for two days. Stay away too long and it goes cold — no income at all until you square it out of pocket, though the envelope stops below a full till so coming back always covers it. That's the deal, not a fault: a business wants an owner who shows up. If you can't carry it, close it up and the pad stops.
Renown · Notoriety · Scrutiny
Reputations that follow you: renown is your nightlife legend; notoriety heats a club toward a raid; scrutiny is the Bureau's file on you. Watched heat — you can't just wait it out.
The Wire
Information you buy with $OMR: tap a rival to see what they're holding and whether they're hunting you; sweep your own lines clean; subscribe to the Street Wire for forecasts and threat chatter.
